requirement: Sanitize untrusted HTML to an allowlist of tags and attributes, dropping executable content and unsafe link schemes.
skeleton: Allowlist constants, _safe_url and _clean_attrs helpers, and sanitize walking every tag to decompose, unwrap or clean it.
caption: An HTML sanitizer using bs4 BeautifulSoup, Comment and Tag with urllib.parse urlsplit. sanitize removes comments, decomposes script, style, iframe and object together with their content, unwraps any tag outside the allowlist so its text survives, and strips every attribute except href and title on links. An href whose scheme is not http, https, mailto or relative is removed, and links that keep an href get rel nofollow noopener. It raises no exceptions. The fixture asserts kept markup, unwrapped tags, dropped dangerous content, attribute filtering, unsafe URL removal and comment removal.

constraints: script, style, iframe and object are dropped with their content
Unknown tags are unwrapped and keep their text
Only href and title survive, and only on a
Only http, https, mailto and relative hrefs are kept
Links with an href get rel nofollow noopener

rationale.teaches: Default-deny: decompose executable containers, unwrap unknown tags, and filter attributes and URL schemes against allowlists.
rationale.why: Blocklist sanitizers miss comments, data URLs and script bodies that survive unwrapping, which leads to stored XSS.

ops.docstring: Sanitize user HTML down to an allowlist of tags and attributes.

ops.stmt: from bs4 import BeautifulSoup, Comment, Tag

candidates.why_wrong: Script bodies survive because dangerous tags are unwrapped, not decomposed.
HTML comments are left in the output.
javascript and data hrefs are kept on links.
The data scheme is allowlisted, so data URLs survive.
Kept links do not get rel nofollow noopener.
